dedupe_keys.name: disaster information management system of sri lanka desinventar disaster management centre

description: The Disaster Information Management System of Sri Lanka is a DesInventar database of past disaster incidents from 1974 onwards, developed by the Disaster Management Centre of the Ministry of Disaster Management with technical and financial support from the UNDP disaster risk management programme and the UNDP Regional Centre in Bangkok. The site describes it as a sustainable arrangement for the systematic collection, documentation and analysis of data on losses caused by natural and human-made disasters, and links a querying system with basic data on the effects of many disaster types. It documents data sources (print media, government and non-governmental organisations and research bodies), the collection process, data validation, disaster definitions, incident reporting formats and a user manual, and it has district pages and a disaster event profile of Sri Lanka summarising patterns of floods, landslides, droughts, extreme winds and lightning by season and district. Access to the query system is free; no licence is stated. Caveats: the home page shows a last update of 30 June 2017 for its site information, data entry needs a login, and past records depend on media and agency reports. Coverage is Sri Lanka by district. It supports historical event analysis and hazard exposure studies for roads, houses and other infrastructure; related records are the global DesInventar Sendai database and InaRISK of Indonesia.
